changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 5 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/10864-app-shell-spec-floor.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` — edited by this change

  > `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` imports `predicateSlotRefusal` from `@objectstack/spec/automation`; `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/simulator/flow-sim-validate.ts` imports `structuralConditionRefusal` from the same subpath plus `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED` and `EvaluatedExpressionSchema` from `@objectstack/spec/shared`. `@objectstack/spec` was declared as `^17.3.0`, so any resolution landing on 17.3.0 (which the range allows) gets a module that names exports its own declared spec dependency does not have.

### `.changeset/5920-flow-runner-translation-overlay.md`

- names `screen-spec.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/screen-spec.ts` — edited by this change

  > ⚠️ **Dated note, 2026-09-28 — the declared floor has since moved again — objectui#10864.** At this change `@object-ui/app-shell` declared `^17.3.0`, and the paragraph above is kept as the reading of that change: `17.3.0` was in fact the first release exporting the resolver family this fix uses. Later in this same release the floor was raised again, to `^17.4.0`, because two other shipped app-shell sources (`screen-spec.ts`, `flow-sim-validate.ts`) import four symbols (`predicateSlotRefusal`, `structuralConditionRefusal`, `EVALUATED_EXPRESSION_SOURCE_REQUIRED`, `EvaluatedExpressionSchema`) that `17.3.0` does not export — a defect this changeset's own range did not introduce and did not need to guard against. `@object-ui/app-shell` now declares `^17.4.0`.

### `.changeset/6310-designer-formula-key-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`) in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, a different and live key belonging to metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector` — the surface that still authors formula expressions.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `52bf34824` (merge-base with origin/main): 4 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1812 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2422 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36724857916)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f370557a38cbb3f249cac3a4eb5de5afc17bf066`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #11190 (body; triage `5909747834`; claim `5909829215`; dev report `5912737920` — the card carries no earlier record), PR #11219 (body, 5 files, the net diff against `main`), the head's check-runs (`filter=latest`, read at 2026-09-30T14:09Z), and head-side file reads for context (`ScreenView.tsx`, `screen-spec.ts`, `ScreenPreview.tsx`, `FlowSimulatorPanel.tsx`, `simulator/flow-simulator.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `views/index.ts`, `package.json`; objectstack `0f6dcac5e9`'s `contracts/automation-service.ts`, `automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts`, `service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts`; the compare API for the merge). Nothing built, run or re-run.

Check-runs on the head: 43, every one completed — 40 success, 3 skipped (`Test (coverage)`, the coverage-shard matrix job, `dependabot`; none is a gate for this PR), 0 failure. The gates the review leans on are all success: `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Spec Main Shape Gate` (green on this head, as expected after objectui#11206's repair came in with the merge), `Test` with `Test (shard 1/8)` through `Test (shard 8/8)`, `Test (dist pins)`, `Build & E2E`, `Line Citation Gate`, `Inert vi.mock Specifier Check`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Control Byte Scan`, and the five changeset gates named in ②.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise on base `846cec0ef`: right.** The base `toScreenFields` (the diff's removed lines) carried `name` / `label` / `type` / `required` / `visibleWhen` and objectui#11188's `min` / `max` / `inlineHelpText` / `reference`, nothing else. `ScreenFieldInput` takes its `Select` branch only when `field.options` is a non-empty array, so app-todo's two `type: 'select'` fields fell through to the text `Input`; a `date` input has no textbox role. The count 0 / 4 / 0 against the runtime's 2 / 2 / 1 is what the code yields. The Proxy probe's 12-key set is every key `ScreenView.tsx` reads (`name` `label` `type` `required` `options` `placeholder` `min` `max` `inlineHelpText` `reference` in `ScreenView` / `ScreenFieldInput`, `defaultValue` in `initialScreenValues`, `visibleWhen` in `visibleScreenFields`), and the spec's `ScreenFieldSpec` at `0f6dcac5e9` declares exactly those 12 keys.
- **One list: right.** `ScreenFieldCarry` is a mapped type over `keyof ScreenFieldSpec` with `-?`, and `SCREEN_FIELD_CARRY` is an object literal annotated with it: a dropped entry is TS2741, an entry the spec lacks is an excess-property error, and `SCREEN_FIELD_KEYS = Object.keys(SCREEN_FIELD_CARRY)` is therefore the spec's own key set at runtime with no second spelling. A key the spec adds widens `keyof ScreenFieldSpec`, the mapped type gains a required entry, and the same literal fails — so the ablation (`options` dropped → TS2741, 2 pins red) and the reverse probe (`futureKey` → TS2741) are what the types yield, and the pin's `Required` literal over `ScreenFieldSpec` is a second compile-time pin in the test tsconfig. Accept-set: the spec's `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` is untouched; the preview stops dropping three keys the spec already admits. Nothing widens.
- **Typed carry / malformed value: right, as declared.** `placeholder` string-only; `options` only when every entry is a non-array object with a string `label` (`value` unchecked, as the spec types it `unknown`); `defaultValue` anything but `undefined`, `null` included. That is the executor's own projection at `0f6dcac5e9` (`screen-nodes.ts`: `required: f.required === true`, `options` forwarded as-is, `defaultValue` interpolated only when not `undefined`, `placeholder` forwarded), and the authoring schema (`strictObject`; `placeholder: z.string()`; option `label: z.string()`) refuses every malformed shape at registration, so a value the preview drops is one no run ever renders. The drop is NOT the consumer-side tolerance objectui AGENTS.md #0.1 forbids: the projection accepts nothing the spec refuses and coerces nothing — it renders less, never more — and it is the pre-existing "a half-typed row adds nothing" rule PR objectui#11188 carried under an accepted amendment, on a live-typing surface where a half-typed row is the transient state. Registration is where a malformed row is diagnosed; declared in the PR's Acceptance notes (a half-typed `options` entry shows as a text box). Acceptable; not a finding.
- **`defaultValue` as written: this is the ruling** (`5909747834`, "show the literal with a marker"). The control is seeded through the unchanged `initialScreenValues`; `holdsTemplateToken` reads `TEMPLATE_TOKEN` (`/\{([^{}]+)\}/g`), the same regex the engine's `interpolateString` substitutes and the simulator's `interpolate` mirrors, and walks strings, arrays and plain objects as the engine's `interpolate` walks them; the marker is one `li[data-default-template]` per visible field, the localized sentence naming the field plus the template in a `code` span; `interpolate` is never applied to a default, `variables` or not (pinned with `variables` holding `customer: 'Acme'`). A default with no reference (app-todo's `'normal'`) seeds the select and gets no line — what the run shows too. Right.
- **`structKey` with `defaultValue`: within "as far as the literal needs it".** `ScreenFormPreview` seeds `values` once (`useState` over `initialScreenValues`), so without the key an edited default would leave the control on the stale seed while the marker line, derived from `spec` each render, showed the new template — the literal and its marker would disagree. `JSON.stringify` on a JSON-sourced config value is safe; typing still survives a label/title-only edit and resets on a default edit, which is the seed applying. Declared (deviation 2). Right.
- **Key-less control: holds from the code.** A row with no carried key yields `{ name, required: false }`; the base added `label: undefined` / `type: undefined` own-keys, which the renderer reads as `f.label || f.name` and `field.type || 'text'` either way; no `defaultValue`, so no marker list; `structKey` reads `f.type ?? ''` and `''` for an absent default. The byte-identical HTML the dev measured for five key-less fields is what the code yields; the pin covers the bare text box.
- **Merge: clean.** `f370557a3` against its first parent `f2c393e9d` is 51 files whose blobs are identical to `846cec0ef...0389650f3`'s 51 (compare API), none of this PR's five: the merge brought only `main`'s own changes, objectui#11206's repair included. `i18n.ts`: this PR adds one row after `engine.screenPreview.hiddenOther` in each table (head :1320 en, :4311 zh); PR objectui#11214 (`52bf34824`) edited the `page:header.breadcrumb` rows at :769 and :3728 — disjoint hunks in both tables, so the queue's three-way merge does not conflict; GitHub's computed state on the PR against `52bf34824` reads `mergeable: true`, `mergeable_state: clean`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11190-screen-preview-field-projection.md` declares `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. The diff publishes nothing: `previews/screen-spec.ts`'s new exports (`defaultValueTemplates`, `DefaultValueTemplate`) and `ScreenPreview.tsx` are unreachable from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts` (it re-exports `FlowRunner` and the `ScreenSpec` / `ScreenFieldSpec` types through `views/index.ts`, plus the metadata-admin pages and registries — not the previews module, not `ScreenView`); the package `exports` map is `.` alone; `ScreenPreviewProps` and `ScreenPreviewNode` are unchanged; no spec schema, prop, type or accepted set moves. A behaviour fix inside an internal projection: patch is the level. The claim's Clause-② `no` line holds for the reason it gives ("an internal projection. No schema, prop, type or accepted set moves"). Changeset gates on the head: Changeset Declaration, Changeset Bump Policy, Changeset Fixed Group Check, Changeset Claim Re-read, Changeset Overwrite Report — all success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`metadata-admin/i18n.ts` outside the claim's surface: declared properly, and minimal.** Named in the report's deviation 1 and in the PR's Acceptance notes with the reason: the order (triage `5909747834`) requires a marker, and the preview's own words read the designer table (objectui#10848; the `check-i18n-call-site-keys` and designer-table-parity gates), so the breach is the order's own and an escalation would have returned the same answer. One en row and one zh row is the fewest the parity gate admits, placed in the existing `engine.screenPreview.*` block; the zh row's ASCII comma and colon match its neighbours (`engine.screenPreview.empty`, `engine.flowSim.note.*`). Answered.
- **`packages/app-shell/src/views/` not run whole locally (520 s timeout):** the head's `Test (shard 1/8 … 8/8)` and `Type Check` runs answer it — all eight shards and `Type Check` completed success on `f370557a3`, so the narrowing the dev declared is closed by CI. Answered.
